method_evidence.claim: MaterialMVP is a one-stage framework that generates PBR textures from image prompts via multi-view PBR diffusion.
method_evidence.anchor: We present MaterialMVP, a novel one-stage framework that generates high-quality PBR textures for 3D meshes from image prompts. We extend the conventional multi-view diffusion to a multi-view PBR diffusion process, generating consistent albedo, metallic, and roughness maps across multiple views.

method_evidence.claim: An additional perturbed reference image is used during training for stable texture generation.
method_evidence.anchor: We also incorporate an additional perturbed reference image during training, ensuring stable texture generation in varying lighting conditions or unstable viewpoints.

experiment_evidence.claim: MaterialMVP achieves leading performance in FID, LPIPS, CMMD, CLIP-I, and CLIP-FID metrics.
Ablation shows one-stage generation outperforms two-stage (SuperMat) in material estimation.
experiment_evidence.value: end-to-end generation better suited; SuperMat renders glass/metal with plastic-like appearance

experiment_evidence.claim: Without consistency loss, model mispredicts materials with excessively high metallic properties.
experiment_evidence.value: model frequently mispredicts materials with excessively high metallic properties

experiment_evidence.claim: Without MCAA, misaligned albedo and MR maps lead to blurred textures.
experiment_evidence.value: variant without MCAA produces misaligned albedo and MR maps in detailed regions, ultimately leading to blurred textures

figure_table_roles.label: fig: re-light
figure_table_roles.caption: We show PBR textures for two meshes with image prompts and display them under various environmental illuminations. The results demonstrate high accuracy in our PBR textures and the ability to remain unaffected by the input image's lighting.

figure_table_roles.label: fig: ablation
figure_table_roles.caption: We ablate the one-stage generation scheme, the consistency loss, and the MCAA, validating the effectiveness of our method in generating high-quality and semantically accurate textures, as well as eliminating blurring artifacts caused by PBR misalignment.
